The May 21 off-cycle bonus run, $12,682.00, was deposited June 5, 8 calendar days after its May 28 due date: $634.10 at 5% is owed on the actual paydays even after the Schedule B. The reply asks for the Automatic Exemption from Penalty on the clean twelve-quarter history. The reasonable-cause statement drafted as a fallback is weak: the run was not released for tax filing, an oversight, and the IRS says mistakes and reliance on others generally do not qualify. A person decides whether to send it; if sent, the President signs it under penalty of perjury.

For 2026 quarterly returns the IRS applies the Automatic Exemption from Penalty, not First Time Abate. On the client's records Q2 2023 to Q1 2026 qualify: all twelve returns on time and paid, all deposits by EFTPS, and the one penalty (Q1 2024, $388.42) abated for reasonable cause, which does not count. AEP is applied when the original return processes, and no AEP letter came for Q2; whether the IRS will apply it to the remaining penalty after the Schedule B, and how many FTD waivers its own records show (four or more disqualify), are for a person to confirm with the IRS once Form 2848 is on file.

The controller says Northline Payroll Services filed the Q3 2026 Form 941 on October 30 with the same monthly box on line 16 and no Schedule B. Expect a CP207 for Q3 as well. A person prepares the Q3 Schedule B from the Q3 payroll and sends it now, has the provider switch its Form 941 module to semiweekly before the Q4 return due February 1, 2027, and sets a control so off-cycle runs are released for tax filing on the day they are paid.

No Form 2848 or Form 8821 is on file for F1 Finance. Until Celeste Whitford signs a Form 2848 for Form 941, 2026 periods, F1 Finance cannot discuss the account with the IRS or file Form 843 for HANGS; the reply itself is signed and mailed by HANGS.
